1.explanation:
1. We import Accordion and AccordionItem from carbon-components-react.  
2. We pass the new boolean prop `isFlush` on the `<Accordion>` component.  
3. When `isFlush` is true, the component should apply a CSS modifier that strips out the default padding-left on both the header and content areas so that the text sits exactly flush to the divider lines (in both closed and open states).  
4. If your version of the library doesn’t yet wire up the flush styles, you can manually override the CSS as shown in the commented-out snippet above.
1.bug_scenario: In this scenario we want to render an Accordion whose headers and body content sit flush to the left divider lines (i.e. remove the default left padding). When the accordion is closed, the titles should align exactly with the divider. When opened, both the title and the body text should remain flush.
